proposal.title: Leaked transcript reports Szijjártó briefed Lavrov on Ukraine’s EU accession talks
proposal.description_short: Reports say Hungary’s Szijjártó briefed Russia’s Lavrov during 2023 EU talks on Ukraine’s accession.
proposal.description_medium: VSquare and Euronews reported in April 2026 that a published transcript of a December 14, 2023 call shows Hungary’s Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó briefing Russia’s Sergey Lavrov during European Council discussions of Ukraine’s EU accession. The accounts describe conversation about negotiations and minority-rights language. They do not establish that the call blocked accession: the Council’s published conclusions say leaders decided to open negotiations that day. No Trump connection is documented.
proposal.description_long: VSquare and Euronews reported in April 2026 on leaked recordings and transcripts of conversations between Hungarian Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov. VSquare dates one call to December 14, 2023, during a European Council meeting in Brussels about opening EU accession negotiations with Ukraine. Its transcript says Szijjártó described Hungary’s position and the negotiations; Lavrov asked about the compromise language on national minorities, and Szijjártó said he would send the relevant document through Hungary’s embassy in Moscow. Euronews separately describes the call as a briefing to Lavrov during the leaders’ debate over opening accession talks. These reports support a bounded account of a reported exchange, not the original claim that the officials coordinated successfully to block Ukraine’s EU path. The European Council’s official conclusions for that meeting state that leaders decided to open accession negotiations with Ukraine. The cited reporting does not independently authenticate the leaked recording, and none of these sources connects the call to Donald Trump. The proposed title and descriptions therefore attribute the account to published reporting and avoid presenting either a successful blockade or a Trump role as established fact.

evidence_map.supports: VSquare reports that on December 14, 2023, Szijjártó called Lavrov during a European Council break, described Hungary’s plan/negotiations, discussed minority-rights language, and offered to send the relevant EU document via Hungary’s Moscow embassy.
Euronews independently reports on the leaked transcript and describes Szijjártó briefing Lavrov during the December 14, 2023 EU leaders’ discussion of Ukraine accession talks.
Official European Council conclusions state that leaders decided to open accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova; this contradicts treating a successful blockade as the outcome.
